result.summary: Reviewed the current state of lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex (git diff main, both oidcc calls unchanged, rescue/catch appended to the def) against the approved design, ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis, and codebase precedent. IDIOM: the rescue/catch is attached directly to the `def ... do ... end` as function-clause sugar (no nested `try do` block, no extracted helper) -- this is the correct shape. NOTE: the design doc cites the precedent as `lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex:250-254` (safe_to_existing_atom/1), but that function does not exist anywhere in authorization.ex -- I verified by grep across lib/. The actual precedent (same `def ... rescue ArgumentError -> nil end` shape, same line numbers 250-254) lives in lib/letflow/engine/service_task.ex:250-254 and is duplicated in lib/letflow/routers/definitions.ex:448-452. This is a design-doc citation error (wrong file name), not an implementation defect -- the implementation independently matches the REAL precedent's shape correctly, so it does not block this gate, but the citation should be corrected for future readers. SUPERVISION: not applicable -- no process/supervision-tree changes in this diff, pure function-level exception handling. SCOPE: @type crash_reason and @spec exactly match design section 3/5, no undesigned abstractions, no helper functions extracted beyond what the design specifies, AuthPipeline is correctly left untouched (confirmed by diff -- only oidcc.ex changed) matching design section 3a's explicit no-change finding. TYPE-SAFETY (non-blocking observation, not filed as an issue): `crash_reason`'s `classification: module() | atom()` is the loosest possible atom typing and is never referenced by the function's own @spec (which uses bare `term()` for the error case, per design section 5's explicit text) -- the real safety guarantee here is structural/by-construction in the code (classification can only ever be an exception's __struct__ or one of two fixed constants or an already-atom reason), not enforced by the type system, but tightening it further isn't practical (rescue branch's `exception.__struct__` is an open set by nature) so I did not file this as a type-safety issue -- it's marginal enough not to be worth queuing as claimable work. DEAD CODE: none -- `require Logger` is used, no unused variables/aliases, `crash_reason` type is unused by any @spec but this produces no compiler warning (confirmed: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exits 0) and is standard practice for a documentation-only public @type. MODULEDOC/@doc: corrected text matches design section 6 verbatim. ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis (unhandled CaseClauseError from jose_base64url.decode!/2 on non-base64url raw_token, propagating through AuthPipeline to a raw 500) is fully addressed: both oidcc calls are now covered by one rescue/catch boundary that always terminates in a well-formed {:error, {:verifier_crashed, %{...}}} tuple matching AuthPipeline's existing {:error, {:verify, reason}} -> 401 collapse, unchanged. Verdict: PASS, no BLOCKERs, one non-blocking documentation-accuracy note (design doc's precedent citation should be corrected to service_task.ex or definitions.ex, not authorization.ex).
